text:
B: Hello. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah. Hiya.
B: I'm Abena. Thornton Heath, in Croydon.
A: Liam. Walsall.
B: You look tired, Liam.
A: Yeah. Come off nights this morning. Four in a row.
B: What is the work?
A: IT at a parcel depot, by the M6. Scanners, label printers, the PCs on the sort lines, the Wi-Fi.
B: So when something breaks, they call you.
A: Yeah. Usually about three in the morning. What do you do?
B: Practice administrator at a GP surgery. Rota, letters, referrals, the systems. And our system goes down sometimes. EMIS. The practice manager rings a number and waits on hold for forty minutes, and nobody in the building knows what to do.
A: Is it the system, or your network?
B: I don't know. That's the honest answer.
A: Nine times out of ten it's the network. There's a router in a cupboard that nobody's touched since it went in, and somebody unplugs it to charge their phone.
B: ...There is a cupboard.
A: Yeah. Check the cupboard.
B: I'll look on Monday. And I'll label it.
A: [laughs] Label it, yeah.
B: What do you do when you're not working?
A: Fix stuff. I buy broken electronics off Marketplace, sort them, sell them on. Got a graphics card last week for ninety quid. The fan was dead, a new one was a fiver, and it'll go for two-fifty.
B: Does the man you bought it from know it was only the fan?
A: Er... no. He set the price.
B: Hm.
A: I'm not lying to him. He just didn't check.
B: That's business, I suppose. I keep the finance records at church, and I wouldn't want it in my books. But I know it's business.
A: Fair.
B: What is the money for?
A: House. Me and my wife are renting. We want to buy before we have kids.
B: Good. We've been buying ours for fifteen years, and I want to finish it early. Every bit extra, I put on the mortgage.
A: Overpayments. Yeah, Jade's always on about that.
B: Jade is right. Listen to her. Don't spend it all on computers.
A: [laughs] Bit, maybe.
B: There was a dog toy in your photo.
A: Diesel. Staffie cross. He's chewed the settee cushion again.
B: Again.
A: Third one.
B: Then the settee is losing.
A: Yeah. It is.
B: Is he trained at all?
A: Sort of. He sits if there's a sausage involved.
B: My husband is the same.
A: [laughs] Yeah?
B: More or less. He falls asleep on the settee in front of the news every night, but he—
